discovery: Discovery of geometric and topological phases in quantum mechanics (the Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase)

nominees.name: Yakir Aharonov
nominees.affiliation: Chapman University, USA, and Tel Aviv University, Israel

motivation: Aharonov (with the late David Bohm, 1959) showed that electromagnetic potentials have direct physical effects on charged particles moving only through field-free regions. Experiments, most decisively Tonomura's, confirmed this. Berry (1984) showed that any quantum system carried adiabatically around a closed loop in parameter space picks up a geometric phase that depends only on the loop's geometry. Aharonov and Anandan later extended this to non-adiabatic evolution. These insights were once dismissed as questions about unobservable phases or potentials. They have since become a cornerstone of modern physics. Geometric phases underlie the topological band theory behind the quantum Hall effects and topological insulators, the modern theory of polarization, and anomalous transport. They are also central to holonomic quantum gates, atom interferometry and photonics. Few conceptual discoveries have reshaped so many experimental fields so thoroughly, and the main protagonists deserve recognition while they are still living.
